```text
1	# training
2	
3	The offline pipeline: how marvin self-play recordings become training data, and the model that consumes them.
4	
5	## 1. Data flow
6	
7	Recap (full diagram in [architecture.md](architecture.md)):
8	
9	```
10	perf-log capture (.bin)
11	    │  contains: SESSION + DETECTOR + ACTUATOR + FRETBOARD_RAW
12	    │
13	    ▼
14	marvin-perf  export-ml --labels=actuator capture.bin out.csv
15	    │
16	    ▼
17	SensiML CSV (per-row: 5 ADC + 6 labels)
18	    │
19	    ▼
20	host training (PyTorch / MPLAB ML)
21	```
22	
23	## 2. New label source in the SensiML exporter
24	
25	Modify [tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/exporters/sensiml_csv.py](../../marvin-perf/marvin_perf/exporters/sensiml_csv.py) to add an `--labels=actuator` mode (the current `pressed_mask` path stays as `--labels=detector` for back-compat):
26	
27	- Track the most recent `Actuator` record alongside `last_detector` (decoder already exists at [tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/records.py:300](../../marvin-perf/marvin_perf/records.py)).
28	- Forward-fill `Actuator.intended_mask` onto each `FretboardRaw` row, emitting frets at bits 0..4 verbatim and a **collapsed strum bit** = `((intended_mask >> 5) | (intended_mask >> 6)) & 1` (logical OR of strum-down and strum-up).
29	- Emit a per-export stat `n_strum_events` so we can verify strum-bit density on a captured corpus.
30	
31	The collapse is a property of *this* exporter mode, not the raw capture. `PERF_REC_ACTUATOR` records both strum bits as marvin emitted them; a future training corpus that includes human-trainer data (where alternating up/down is meaningful as ergonomic ground truth) keeps both bits intact on disk and can either be exported through the same collapse for this model, or through a future direction-aware exporter for a different model variant.
32	
33	## 3. CSV schema
34	
35	```
36	timestamp,
37	ph_green, ph_red, ph_yellow, ph_blue, ph_orange,
38	fret_green, fret_red, fret_yellow, fret_blue, fret_orange,
39	strum
40	```
41	
42	Same row cadence as today (one row per `FretboardRaw` ≈ 240 Hz).
43	
44	## 4. Capture protocol
45	
46	A training corpus is a set of marvin self-play perf-log captures **at a single difficulty (Expert for v1)** across song variety. Each capture must have all of `SESSION + DETECTOR + ACTUATOR + FRETBOARD_RAW` enabled in the `PERF_CMD_SET_TYPE_MASK`.
47	
48	A held-out song is reserved for offline validation; the same held-out set is reused across training iterations so per-iteration metrics are comparable.
49	
50	> **Why single-difficulty.** If the game highway's scroll speed varies with difficulty, the photo-dip→strum delay is `(pixel gap photo-row→CV-row)/scroll_speed + 220 ms` — inversely dependent on scroll speed. With 5 sensors at one screen row and no difficulty input, mixing difficulties makes identical inputs map to different correct delays: an *ill-posed* regression, not merely an under-sampled one. So v1 fixes difficulty to Expert (densest strum signal, shortest delay → smallest window). If scroll speed turns out constant across difficulties, difficulties can be merged later at no cost. Eventual multi-difficulty support is one-model-per-difficulty (difficulty selected at runtime from marvin's game-state controller), or a dedicated fret-line scroll-speed sensor — see journal open questions.
51	
52	## 5. Model
53	
54	### 5.1 Recommended baseline
55	
56	- **Input:** 5 ADC channels × N samples causal window @ 240 Hz, windowed **by row index** (each CSV row is one true 240 Hz sample; the `timestamp` column is bursty — see journal), int16 → int8 after normalisation. Size N from the measured photo→strum lag (§5.2), starting near 60 (250 ms).
57	- **Output:** 6 sigmoids during training (independent BCE per bit) — 5 frets + 1 collapsed strum; thresholded to binary at deploy. The runtime stage maps the strum bit into the wire byte's bit 5 (strum-down); bit 6 stays 0.
58	- **Architecture (primary):** tiny causal 1D-CNN — two conv layers ~8 channels, kernel 5–7, dilation `[1, 4]`, causal padding, → dense → 6 sigmoids. Quantise to int8. This is the primary path (see journal decision log): the strum-timing problem is a sequence/event problem the auto-pipeline's windowed-feature + tree/ensemble shape handles poorly.
59	- **MPLAB ML / SensiML (later demonstration track):** windowed feature extractor (MAV, std, slope, peak, simple FIR taps) feeding a gradient-boosted ensemble or tiny dense head. SensiML targets exactly this MCU class, so once a known-good model shape exists it's a strong "here's the Microchip-tooling path" comparison — but it is **not** the v1 critical path.
60	
61	### 5.2 Sizing the window: measure, don't guess
62	
63	`TP_STRUM_DELAY_MS = 220` ([timing_pipeline.c:21](../../../firmware/marvin/default/src/actuator/timing_pipeline.c)) is only the *fixed* part of the delay; the photo→strum lag also includes scroll-time from the photo row to marvin's CV row. With difficulty fixed (§4) that total lag is a constant we **measure** from real data by cross-correlating photo dips against strum events (the `edge-ai lag` utility). Size the causal window to span the measured lag plus margin, then sweep narrowly around it (e.g. measured ±1–2 samples of window) rather than blind-sweeping 125/250/400 ms — see [review.md Q3](review.md#q3-look-ahead-vs-now-cast).
64	
65	### 5.3 Quantisation
66	
67	int8 weights, int16 activations during the conv layers, int8 at the output. The intended deployment target has no FPU; floating-point inference is a non-starter. If the offline phase chooses to revisit the deployment target, the quantisation choice may relax.
68	
69	## 6. Loss
70	
71	Independent BCE per output bit, weighted to compensate for class imbalance:
72	
73	- Fret bits are dense (often 1 for many ticks per chord); near-1:1 weighting works.
74	- The strum bit is sparse — measured at **~5.8 %** of samples on the first real Expert capture (551 strum events / 3 496 active rows over 59 958 rows); weight strongly (≈15–20× positive, i.e. the inverse class frequency) to avoid the trivial "always 0" minimum. Focal loss is a sane alternative if simple weighting plateaus.
75	
76	If per-bit independence produces poor strum timing, switch to a multi-class head over common chord shapes — see [review.md §alternatives](review.md#12-alternatives-considered).
77
```

```text
1	# review
2	
3	This is the document to push back on. Three categories: things we know can fail (risks), forks we haven't decided (open questions), and shapes we explicitly rejected (alternatives).
4	
5	## Risks
6	
7	- **Strum class imbalance.** The collapsed strum bit is 1 for ≤2 ticks per chord — well under 5% of samples. Weighted BCE / focal loss / oversampling required; verify in phase 2 that the model isn't degenerating to "always 0".
8	- **Window-too-short failure mode.** If 250 ms doesn't span the photo-dip-to-strum-bit delay across difficulty levels (Expert scrolls faster — photo dip is closer to the strum), strum-bit accuracy collapses. Sweep window in phase 2 (125 / 250 / 400 ms).
9	- **Per-bit independence vs. chord structure.** Treating bits as independent sigmoids ignores that real chords occupy a tiny subset of the 2⁶ space. If accuracy is poor, switch to a multi-class head over common chord shapes — see [§alternatives](#12-alternatives-considered).
10	- **Multi-difficulty is ill-posed, not just out-of-distribution (resolved → single-difficulty v1).** Original guidance here was "train on Easy + Medium + Expert." That is wrong if scroll speed varies with difficulty: the photo→strum lag = `(pixel gap photo-row→CV-row)/scroll_speed + 220 ms`, so the same photo-dip pattern maps to *different* correct delays across difficulties. With 5 sensors at one row and no difficulty input, the model can't disambiguate — mixing difficulties is an ill-posed regression more data can't fix. **Resolution:** v1 trains on Expert only (see journal decision log + [training.md §4](training.md)). Per-difficulty models, or a fret-line scroll-speed sensor ([Q5](#q5-photoxistor-placement)), are the multi-difficulty routes for later.
11	- **Inheriting marvin's bugs.** Distillation can't beat the teacher. Mistimed strums in marvin become mistimed strums in the AI. Acceptable for v1; future work could layer human-play recordings on top (see [Q4](#q4-strike-line-cv-detector-as-alternative-label-source)).
12	- **CDC + RTOS jitter in labels, and a cross-stream pairing skew.** `PERF_REC_ACTUATOR` timestamps the moment marvin *emits* the command, not the moment fretboard asserts the GPIO. Sharper still: the label is stamped on the **send** path and the feature (`FRETBOARD_RAW`) on the **receive** path — opposite USB-CDC directions with independent latency/jitter — so the exporter's forward-fill pairs them with an unknown, varying skew. Probably fine for v1 (fretboard saw that same jitter at runtime), but it's a candidate accuracy ceiling. The clean fix is to pair sensor + applied-actuator-state atomically on the fretboard and carry both on the wire (fretboard journal open-questions #3/#4; edge-ai journal). Measure the impact in phase 2 before committing to the firmware change.
13	
14	## Open questions
15	
16	> Reviewers: each of these is a real fork. Speak up *before* phase 1 lands.
17	
18	<a id="q1-hold-vs-edge-channel-per-fret"></a>
19	### Q1: Hold vs. edge channel per fret — add HW now, or wait?
20	
21	The current 5-channel ADC at 240 Hz may alias on fast transients. Two ways to add information:
22	
23	- **(a)** Two photoxistors per fret at *different* screen rows — gives the model an intrinsic "note approaching" + "note here" pair, doubling temporal resolution at hardware cost.
24	- **(b)** One extra photoxistor per fret with a colour filter, mimicking `cv_marvin_v1`'s colour-edge channel — separates "any brightness here" from "specifically a green note here".
25	
26	Either doubles the ADC scan time. Bias is to start with the existing 5 channels and only add HW if phase 2 shows the model is starved for input.
27	
28	<a id="q2-ar-feedback"></a>
29	### Q2: AR feedback — let the model see its own past output?
30	
31	Most fret-bit predictions at time `T` are highly correlated with the prediction at `T-1` (held notes). An AR model could be much smaller / more accurate. Cost: a feedback loop at runtime (bugs amplify), and harder training (teacher forcing vs. scheduled sampling). Defer until non-AR baseline is known.
32	
33	<a id="q3-look-ahead-vs-now-cast"></a>
34	### Q3: Window length — measure first, then sweep narrowly
35	
36	Window length is the most important hyperparameter, but with difficulty fixed it need not be a blind sweep. The photo→strum lag is a constant we can **measure** by cross-correlating photo dips against strum events on real data (the `edge-ai lag` utility); size the causal window to span the measured lag + margin, then sweep ±1–2 samples around it. (`TP_STRUM_DELAY_MS = 220` is only the fixed part — the full lag includes scroll-time from the photo row to marvin's CV row.)
37	
38	**Look-ahead vs. now-cast.** Currently formulated as "predict the command at *now*". Could instead predict at `T + K_ms` to cover model+actuator latency. Irrelevant while actuators are GPIOs (latency ≈ 0); revisit when mechanical actuators land (system [SPEC.md §5](../../../SPEC.md), [hardware/actuators/](../../../hardware/actuators/)).
39	
40	<a id="q4-strike-line-cv-detector-as-alternative-label-source"></a>
41	### Q4: Strike-line CV detector as alternative label source?
42	
43	If phase 2 reveals that distillation hits a noise ceiling (CDC jitter + chord-window quantisation), an alternative is to add a `cv_strike_v1` detector on marvin that samples the *strike row* directly at 60 Hz. Cleaner labels for fret state, but loses strum-event timing — would need to re-add a rule-based "strum when strike row goes active". Flag for now, don't build.
44	
45	<a id="q5-photoxistor-placement"></a>
46	### Q5: Phototransistor placement / count — what's optimal?
47	
48	Today's PCB ([hardware/Sensor-LCD5/](../../../hardware/Sensor-LCD5/)) has 5 sensors above the strike line. Optimum-for-this-AI is unknown:
49	
50	- *Higher* on the screen → longer lookahead but more time for the note appearance to change.
51	- *At the strike line* → simplest label (the photo dip *is* the answer) but no anticipation, breaking strum scheduling.
52	- *Two rows* → see [Q1](#q1-hold-vs-edge-channel-per-fret).
53	- *A dedicated fret-line / scroll-speed channel* → a 6th sensor aimed at a column where only the highway's horizontal bar/measure lines pass (not the colored notes). The frequency at which lines cross it **is** the scroll speed — the exact variable single-row note sensors can't observe (see the multi-difficulty risk above). Could let one model span difficulties instead of one-per-difficulty. Open whether a tiny int8 model can actually use it to modulate strum timing. v1 stays 5-channel Expert-only; flagged for future work.
54	
55	Open until phase 2 data tells us which placement makes the model's job easiest.
56	
57	## 12. Alternatives considered
58	
59	Three other shapes were on the table before the current distillation choice landed:
60	
61	- **Shape A — frame classifier with co-located CV.** Model predicts `pressed_mask` from a single ADC sample; labels come from a *new* CV detector at the photoxistor row. Pros: small model, easy to label. Rejected because it still leaves the strum decision outside the AI, and forces mechanical alignment between CV and photoxistors — exactly the problem we're trying to dissolve.
62	- **Shape B — sequence-to-strike-line oracle.** Model takes a causal ADC window, outputs what's at the strike row right now. Labels come from a new strike-row CV detector. Pros: clean physical meaning ("predict the moment of truth"). Rejected because, like A, it doesn't include strum timing — a downstream rule still has to schedule strums. We'd be solving the easier half of the problem twice.
63	- **Shape D — two-head (continuous fret + sparse strum events).** One head for held-note state, one head for `[time-to-strum, mask, dir]` events. Closer to the underlying physics. Rejected as v1 because it's significantly more complex to architect, train, and validate. **Worth revisiting if the per-bit-independence loss in the current shape produces poor strum timing in phase 2** — D's sparse-event head is a natural cure.
64
```

1	# rollout
2	
3	Phased plan with explicit offline / hardware split. Phases 1–4 are entirely offline (Python on a dev PC, no firmware changes). Phase 5 is the first hardware touch.
4	
5	## Offline phases
6	
7	| Phase | Goal | Done when |
8	|---|---|---|
9	| **1. Data pipeline** | Distillation labels available end-to-end | `--labels=actuator` exporter merged in [tools/marvin-perf](../../marvin-perf/); one captured-gameplay CSV inspected and shows plausible fret + strum timing |
10	| **2. Host-side baseline** | Train on PC; validate offline | MPLAB ML / PyTorch model achieves ≥95% per-bit accuracy on held-out song; strum-event timing error p95 ≤ 20 ms (one ADC sample) |
11	
12	### Phase 1 verification
13	
14	Run `marvin-perf export-ml --labels=actuator capture.bin out.csv`; manually inspect:
15	
16	- Row count ≈ 240 × duration_s.
17	- Strum bits sparse (a few %).
18	- Fret bits dense and matching gameplay difficulty.
19	
20	### Phase 2 verification
21	
22	Training script reports per-bit accuracy and strum-event timing distribution on the held-out split. Plot predicted vs. true command stream over a 30 s window; visually verify chord+strum alignment.
23	
24	## Hardware-touching phases
25	
26	| Phase | Goal | Done when |
27	|---|---|---|
28	| **3. On-device port** | Same model running on PIC32 | Inference latency < 1 ms (well inside the 4.17 ms tick); on-device output matches host inference bit-for-bit on a recorded ADC trace (within int8 quant tolerance) |
29	| **4. Side-by-side dry-run** | AI predicts but doesn't drive | New perf-log record `PERF_REC_MODEL_OUT` mirrors `Actuator` shape; recorded alongside marvin's commands; per-tick agreement tracked over a real session |
30	| **5. Cut-over** | AI drives the controller | Fretboard mode-switch flips wire ownership from `cmd_receive` to `model_infer`; gameplay scoring measured against marvin-driven baseline |
31	
32	### Phase 3 verification
33	
34	Unit test feeds a recorded ADC trace through host inference and on-device inference, asserts identical outputs (or ≤1 LSB diff after quant). On-device latency measured from a perf-log timestamp around the inference call.
35	
36	### Phase 4 verification
37	
38	Extend perf-log with `PERF_REC_MODEL_OUT` (mirrors `Actuator` shape); marvin-perf gains a side-by-side viewer; per-tick Hamming distance between model output and marvin output is logged live.
39	
40	### Phase 5 verification
41	
42	Actual game scoring on a fixed song setlist (Easy + Medium + Expert), 5+ runs each: marvin-driven baseline vs. model-driven. Pass if model-driven scores within X% of baseline (X to be set by reviewer).
43	
44	## Gating between offline and hardware phases
45	
46	A reviewer should be able to look at phase 2's metrics — per-bit accuracy, strum-event timing distribution, and a visual side-by-side over a 30 s window — and decide *yes, this is worth porting*. If the metrics are weak, [review.md](review.md) lists the natural pivots: window length sweep, multi-class chord head, two-head event detector, alternative label source. The point of the offline-first split is to take those pivots cheaply, before any on-device work has been spent.
47
```

1	/* Recompute inference. Compiled only when streaming is OFF, so when streaming is
2	 * selected this translation unit is empty and allocates no static buffers (the
3	 * 16ch window-85 s_act alone is ~4 KB) — both modules can coexist in the project. */
4	#include "fretboard_config.h"
5	#if !MODEL_INFER_STREAMING
6	
7	#include "model_infer.h"
8	#include "model_weights.h"
9	
10	#include <stddef.h>
11	#include <string.h>
12	
13	/* Architecture is fixed by the generated header; guard against a mismatched
14	 * regeneration that the hand-written cascade below wouldn't honour. */
15	#if MODEL_N_IN != 5 || MODEL_N_OUT != 6
16	#error "model_infer.c expects 5 ADC inputs and 6 outputs"
17	#endif
18	
19	#define QMAX 127
20	
21	/* The active model. Swappable at runtime (e.g. per difficulty); all candidate
22	 * models share the compile-time dims used to size the scratch below. */
23	static const model_def_t *s_model;
24	
25	/* Input ring: WINDOW newest scans, oldest at window position 0. */
26	static uint16_t s_ring[MODEL_WINDOW][MODEL_N_IN];
27	static uint16_t s_pos;      /* next write slot (== oldest when full) */
28	static uint16_t s_count;    /* samples buffered, saturates at WINDOW */
29	
30	/* Which positions each layer must evaluate to produce the last timestep only
31	 * (recomputed by set_model). Skips the dense per-position conv that would blow
32	 * the 4.17 ms tick. */
33	static uint8_t s_need[MODEL_N_LAYERS][MODEL_WINDOW];
34	
35	/* Scratch: standardised int8 input, and per-layer int8 activations. */
36	static int8_t s_qin[MODEL_WINDOW][MODEL_N_IN];
37	static int8_t s_act[MODEL_N_LAYERS][MODEL_WINDOW][MODEL_CHANNELS];
38	
39	/* Strum monostable state (deploy-time one-shot, model->strum_hold ticks). */
40	static uint32_t s_tick;
41	static uint32_t s_hold_until;
42	static uint32_t s_block_until;
43	static uint8_t  s_prev_strum;
44	
45	static int8_t clamp_i8(int64_t v)
46	{
47	    if (v > QMAX)  return QMAX;
48	    if (v < -QMAX) return -QMAX;
49	    return (int8_t)v;
50	}
51	
52	void model_infer_set_model(const model_def_t *m)
53	{
54	    s_model = m;
55	    if (m == NULL) { return; }
56	
57	    /* Back-propagate the needed positions: the top layer needs only the last
58	     * timestep; each lower layer needs the taps its consumer reads. */
59	    memset(s_need, 0, sizeof(s_need));
60	    s_need[MODEL_N_LAYERS - 1][MODEL_WINDOW - 1] = 1u;
61	    for (int l = MODEL_N_LAYERS - 1; l >= 1; l--)
62	    {
63	        int dil = m->dilation[l];
64	        for (int p = 0; p < MODEL_WINDOW; p++)
65	        {
66	            if (!s_need[l][p]) { continue; }
67	            for (int j = 0; j < MODEL_KERNEL; j++)
68	            {
69	                int pos = p - j * dil;
70	                if (pos >= 0) { s_need[l - 1][pos] = 1u; }
71	            }
72	        }
73	    }
74	}
75	
76	void model_infer_init(void)
77	{
78	    s_pos = 0;
79	    s_count = 0;
80	    s_tick = 0;
81	    s_hold_until = 0;
82	    s_block_until = 0;
83	    s_prev_strum = 0;
84	    model_infer_set_model(MODEL_DEFAULT);
85	}
86	
87	void model_infer_push(const uint16_t adc[5])
88	{
89	    for (int c = 0; c < MODEL_N_IN; c++)
90	    {
91	        s_ring[s_pos][c] = adc[c];
92	    }
93	    s_pos = (uint16_t)((s_pos + 1u) % MODEL_WINDOW);
94	    if (s_count < MODEL_WINDOW) { s_count++; }
95	}
96	
97	/* Causal int8 conv at output position p: out[o] = requant(relu(bias + Σ w·in)).
98	 * Tap k reads input at p-(K-1-k)*dil (the PyTorch causal-left-pad convention).
99	 * `in` is row-major [position][in_stride]. */
100	static void conv_at(const int8_t *w, const int32_t *b, int cin, int dil,
101	                    int32_t mult, int shift, const int8_t *in, int in_stride,
102	                    int p, int8_t out[MODEL_CHANNELS])
103	{
104	    for (int o = 0; o < MODEL_CHANNELS; o++)
105	    {
106	        int32_t acc = b[o];
107	        for (int i = 0; i < cin; i++)
108	        {
109	            const int8_t *wo = &w[(o * cin + i) * MODEL_KERNEL];
110	            for (int k = 0; k < MODEL_KERNEL; k++)
111	            {
112	                int pos = p - (MODEL_KERNEL - 1 - k) * dil;
113	                if (pos < 0) { continue; }
114	                acc += (int32_t)wo[k] * (int32_t)in[pos * in_stride + i];
115	            }
116	        }
117	        if (acc < 0) { acc = 0; }   /* ReLU */
118	        int64_t q = ((int64_t)acc * mult + ((int64_t)1 << (shift - 1))) >> shift;
119	        if (q > QMAX) { q = QMAX; }
120	        out[o] = (int8_t)q;
121	    }
122	}
123	
124	uint8_t model_infer_run(void)
125	{
126	    const model_def_t *m = s_model;
127	    /* Snapshot the ring cursor: when inference runs in the main loop the TC0 ISR
128	     * may push() concurrently. Using a fixed `pos` keeps the window mapping
129	     * stable for this inference; at worst the oldest slot is overwritten mid-run
130	     * (60 samples back — negligible). */
131	    uint16_t pos = s_pos;
132	    if (m == NULL || s_count < MODEL_WINDOW) { return 0u; }
133	
134	    /* Standardise the whole window into int8 (folded mean/std + input scale). */
135	    for (int wpos = 0; wpos < MODEL_WINDOW; wpos++)
136	    {
137	        int ring_idx = (pos + wpos) % MODEL_WINDOW;
138	        for (int c = 0; c < MODEL_N_IN; c++)
139	        {
140	            int64_t v = (int64_t)s_ring[ring_idx][c] * m->m_in[c] - m->b_in[c];
141	            int64_t q = (v + ((int64_t)1 << (m->s_in_shift - 1))) >> m->s_in_shift;
142	            s_qin[wpos][c] = clamp_i8(q);
143	        }
144	    }
145	
146	    /* Conv layers, only at the needed positions. */
147	    for (int l = 0; l < MODEL_N_LAYERS; l++)
148	    {
149	        const int8_t *in = (l == 0) ? &s_qin[0][0] : &s_act[l - 1][0][0];
150	        int in_stride = (l == 0) ? MODEL_N_IN : MODEL_CHANNELS;
151	        for (int p = 0; p < MODEL_WINDOW; p++)
152	        {
153	            if (!s_need[l][p]) { continue; }
154	            conv_at(m->w[l], m->b[l], m->cin[l], m->dilation[l],
155	                    m->req_mult[l], m->req_shift[l], in, in_stride,
156	                    p, s_act[l][p]);
157	        }
158	    }
159	
160	    /* Head on the last timestep: bit = (logit >= threshold), no sigmoid. */
161	    const int8_t *last = &s_act[MODEL_N_LAYERS - 1][MODEL_WINDOW - 1][0];
162	    uint8_t mask = 0u;
163	    int raw_strum = 0;
164	    for (int o = 0; o < MODEL_N_OUT; o++)
165	    {
166	        int32_t acc = m->head_b[o];
167	        for (int i = 0; i < MODEL_CHANNELS; i++)
168	        {
169	            acc += (int32_t)m->head_w[o * MODEL_CHANNELS + i] * (int32_t)last[i];
170	        }
171	        int bit = (acc >= m->head_tq[o]) ? 1 : 0;
172	        if (o < 5) { if (bit) { mask |= (uint8_t)(1u << o); } }
173	        else       { raw_strum = bit; }
174	    }
175	
176	    /* Strum monostable: one pulse per rising edge, model->strum_hold ticks. */
177	    int strum_out;
178	    if (m->strum_hold > 0)
179	    {
180	        uint32_t i = s_tick;
181	        if (raw_strum && !s_prev_strum && i >= s_block_until)
182	        {
183	            s_hold_until  = i + m->strum_hold;
184	            s_block_until = i + m->strum_hold + m->strum_refractory;
185	        }
186	        strum_out = (i < s_hold_until) ? 1 : 0;
187	        s_prev_strum = (uint8_t)raw_strum;
188	        s_tick++;
189	    }
190	    else
191	    {
192	        strum_out = raw_strum;
193	    }
194	    if (strum_out) { mask |= (uint8_t)(1u << 5); }
195	
196	    return mask;
197	}
198	
199	#endif /* !MODEL_INFER_STREAMING */

3	Running log of planning, decisions, open questions, and work-in-progress for the edge-ai distillation effort. Newest entries at the top. For *what edge-ai is* (purpose, the distillation shape, phased rollout), read [`SPEC.md`](SPEC.md) and the doc map there — this journal does not duplicate it.

7	## Current focus

11	End-to-end works: a 16-channel int8 StrumNet, distilled from marvin's hard-mode play across 5 songs, runs standalone on the PIC32CM (no marvin), reads its own photosensors, and drives the controller — playing hard reasonably well on the bench. Deploy model: `--channels 16 --no-holdout --strum-weight 5`, quantised at strum thresh 0.80. Inference in the main loop (not the ISR), 240 Hz sampling, SW0/LED enable toggle.

16	- **Data-sync, schema v4** (`3a6ea3d`): fretboard frame carries `sample_seq` + `applied_mask`; sensor↔label paired atomically on-device (killed the cross-stream skew). `actuator-fb` / `detector-fb` exporter modes; edge-ai loader windows within contiguous `fb_seq` runs. 18	- **Legato fret ceiling fixed end-to-end (2026-06-04).** line-263 released-style commands (`687bb37`) reflashed + confirmed clean play on hardware; old corpus deleted, 5-song hard corpus re-captured (`actuator-fb`). **Overfit A/B verdict — labels are clean AND RF was the limiter:** RF85 `(1,4,16)` overfits slowride-hard to **frets 0.97–0.99 / strum recall 0.97 / p95 16.7 ms** (50k MACs, under budget), vs RF21 `(1,4)` capped at **~0.86** (loss plateau 0.31, can't see back to the photo cue). Strum recall generalises to ~the overfit ceiling (.965 vs .97). **Red is the one laggard (.890)** — not a corpus-coverage gap (slowride red density 26 % is mid-pack); flagged as open follow-up. Old pre-fix baseline for contrast: held-out frets 80–94 %, strum recall ~30 %.

42	## Decision log
43	
44	| Date | Decision | Rationale |
45	|------|----------|-----------|
46	| 2026-06-04 | **Deploy model = 16 channels (not the 8ch training default), trained on the full 5-song corpus (`--no-holdout`), `--strum-weight 5`, 50 epochs; quantised at strum thresh 0.80 / refractory 8.** | 8ch is capacity-limited on the sparse strum class (proven: 8ch overfit strum recall ~.86 vs 64ch ~.99; on hardware the 8ch full-corpus model overstrummed and no threshold fixed it — 0.85 missed real strums *and* still overstrummed, i.e. the precision/recall curve itself was the wall). 16ch lifts the curve (mono .856/.969 → .942/.981) so a threshold lands both. Affordable because inference now runs in the main loop, not the ISR — ~12.5k MACs / ~2–3 ms, 240 Hz sampling unaffected, RAM ~4 KB of 8 KB. `--strum-weight 5` (< the ~8–10 auto) trims the recall bias at the source. Threshold stays a header-only knob (0.80↔0.85 the live range). |
47	| 2026-06-04 | **Corpus + firmware timing pinned at `TP_STRUM_DELAY_MS=300` / `TP_STRUM_PULSE_MS=40` (marvin `8e5d18`, tuned for hard).** The 5-song hard corpus was captured at these values; the model is only valid for the timing it was distilled from — do **not** mix captures from other timing regimes (e.g. the old 220/25) into one corpus. If timing changes again, re-capture the whole corpus. | The deployed model *is* the timing function (photo→fret+strum), so the strum onset it learns is set by `TP_STRUM_DELAY_MS` and the pulse width by `TP_STRUM_PULSE_MS`. Mixing regimes would teach two different photo→strum lags for identical inputs — the same ill-posed averaging as mixing difficulties. No model/architecture change needed for the 220→300/25→40 bump: the RF85 overfit A/B was *itself* run on this 300/40 corpus and fit it (frets 0.99, strum recall 0.97, p95 16.7 ms), which empirically proves RF85 covers this timing's lag; the monostable also normalises the output pulse to `--strum-hold`, so the wider 40 ms label pulse doesn't force a knob change. |
48	| 2026-06-04 | **Default model RF widened to `(1,4,16)` (RF 85) from `(1,4)` (RF 21).** Added a `--dilations` CLI flag; saved in the checkpoint and read back at eval (fallback `(1,4)` for pre-flag checkpoints). | Overfit A/B on clean line-263 `actuator-fb` data (slowride-hard, train==eval): RF21 caps at frets ~0.86 / loss plateau 0.31 — it can't see back to the photo cue ~48 samples before the strike line, so it can't hold the fret. RF85 (50k MACs, under the ~100k budget) recovers to frets 0.97–0.99 / strum recall 0.97 / p95 16.7 ms. Exactly the masked-by-detfb limitation model.md predicted would bite `actuator-fb`. Frets are the headline; widening RF costs ~19k MACs and is well affordable. |
49	| 2026-06-03 | **Primary path is programmatic (PyTorch), not MPLAB ML / SensiML.** MPLAB ML is demoted to an eventual *parallel demonstration* track, not the critical path. Inverts [`training.md` §5.1](training.md), which had the auto-pipeline first. | The hard part of this task is *temporal strum timing* — learning the photo-dip→strum delay over a causal window. SensiML's AutoML is feature-extraction + tree/ensemble over windowed stats: strong at "classify this window," weak at sequence/event-timing, which is exactly the part we care about (and review.md already named a causal 1D-CNN as the fallback). PyTorch gives full control over the window-length sweep (the #1 hyperparameter, [review.md Q3](review.md)), the sparse-strum class weighting, and the custom Phase-2 eval metrics (per-bit accuracy + strum-event timing distribution + visual side-by-side) the gate is judged on. Cost accepted: we own int8 quantisation + the on-device inference C in Phase 3 — tractable for a ≲1 k-MAC, 2-conv model, and the bit-exact control actually helps Phase 3's "matches host inference" gate. MPLAB ML stays valuable later as the Microchip-tooling demonstration once a known-good shape exists. |
50	| 2026-06-03 | **v1 trains on a single difficulty — Expert.** Corpus = many songs at Expert, one held out. NOT mixed-difficulty (which reverses the old [`review.md`](review.md) "train on Easy+Med+Expert" prescription). | If the game's highway scroll speed varies with difficulty, the photo-dip→strum delay = `(pixel gap photo-row→CV-row)/scroll_speed + 220 ms` — the first term is inversely proportional to scroll speed. With 5 sensors at one row and no difficulty input, identical inputs map to different correct delays across difficulties: an ill-posed regression the model can only resolve by averaging (wrong on all). This is an *observability* gap, not a coverage gap, so more mixed data can't fix it. Single-difficulty is low-regret: if scroll speed turns out constant we lose nothing and can merge later; if it varies we've dodged the ill-posed case. Expert chosen for densest strum signal (helps the ~5.8 % rare class) and shortest delay (smallest window). Eventual structure if speed varies: one model per difficulty, difficulty selected at runtime from marvin's game-state controller. |
51	| 2026-06-03 | Phase 1 exporter implemented as a `--labels={detector,actuator}` switch on the existing `export-ml` command rather than a new subcommand. Default stays `detector` (back-compat); `actuator` emits the `fret_*,strum` schema. | The two modes share the whole capture-read / timestamp / forward-fill loop; only the label-source record (`Detector` vs `Actuator`) and the output columns differ. A flag keeps one code path and one set of edge-case handling (missing SESSION, pre-label rows, strict mode). The detector path's CSV bytes are unchanged, so the existing corpus/tooling keeps working. |
52	| 2026-06-03 | `n_strum_events` stat counts **rising edges** (0→1 transitions) of the collapsed strum bit, not strum-active rows. | "Events" = distinct strums, which is the quantity to sanity-check against a song's note count. Per-row density ("a few %") is still eyeballable from the CSV; the rising-edge count is the more information-dense single number and doesn't conflate hold-duration with strum count. |
53	| 2026-06-03 | Collapsed strum bit computed from `Actuator.intended_mask` bits 5\|6 (the doc formula), not from the separate `strum_dir` field. | `intended_mask` is the actual 7-bit wire byte marvin sent (`FretboardLink_Send` value at [fretboard_link.c:430](../../../firmware/marvin/default/src/actuator/fretboard_link.c#L430)); distilling against the byte-on-the-wire is the whole point. `strum_dir` is a redundant convenience enum. Using the mask keeps the label = exactly what fretboard saw. |
54	| 2026-06-03 | ACTUATOR producer wiring confirmed present in marvin firmware before building the exporter. | `PerfLog_EmitActuator` is called unconditionally inside `FretboardLink_Send` ([fretboard_link.c:430](../../../firmware/marvin/default/src/actuator/fretboard_link.c#L430)), which both `timing_pipeline` and `manual_control` drive. Each row is still exactly one true fretboard sample at the fixed 240 Hz rate, so counting rows gives correct, jitter-free windows; slicing by wall-clock timestamp would not. 61	## Open questions
62	
63	> Phase-1-blocking items first; the design forks for phase 2+ live in [`review.md`](review.md).
64	
65	- **[Future hardware — user wants to pursue] 2 photosensors per fret channel (like the CV detector).** Add a second sensor per fret so each channel sees two points along the note's travel (à la marvin's CV detector). Implications: input grows 5→10 channels (`MODEL_N_IN`, the input ring, the input affine — all parameterised already, but the trained model + `model_weights.h` change); two sensors per fret give the model an explicit *velocity/approach* signal (a note dimming sensor A then B encodes speed + direction), which should sharpen onset timing and could reduce the photo→strum lag ambiguity — possibly even let one model span difficulties (relates to the deferred scroll-speed-sensor idea below). Needs: fretboard HW revision (10 ADC inputs / channel mux), a fret_scan update, a wire-format/`FretboardRaw` bump for 10 channels, re-capture the corpus on the new HW, retrain. Big change; the current 5-sensor model is the baseline it must beat. **Discuss scope before building.**
66	
67	- **[Open follow-up] Red fret is the lone laggard (held-out .890 vs ≥.96 for the others).** Consistent across epochs and was joint-weakest in overfit too, so it's real, not noise. *Not* a corpus-coverage gap — slowride red density (26 %) is mid-pack vs the training songs (24–30 %). Hypotheses to test: (a) single-holdout variance — **rotate the holdout** across all five songs and see if the weak fret tracks the song (variance) or stays red (systemic); (b) neighbour confusion — red sits between green/yellow, so check red's false-positives/negatives against green/yellow activity; (c) `ph_red` channel quality (saturation/standardisation stats). Cheapest first move: rotate-holdout cross-val. Carried as a known caveat into Phase 3; confirm whether it actually costs notes against game score before treating it as blocking.
68	
69	- **Need a real self-play capture to close the Phase-1 gate.** The exporter is verified against synthetic records, but the rollout's Phase-1 "done when" requires inspecting one real captured-gameplay CSV. Required record types in the capture's `PERF_CMD_SET_TYPE_MASK`: `SESSION` + `ACTUATOR` + `FRETBOARD_RAW` (the exporter strictly needs only these three); `DETECTOR` recommended for cross-checking `pressed_mask` vs `intended_mask`. The existing files in [`tools/marvin-perf/captures/`](../../marvin-perf/captures/) are *already-exported detector CSVs*, not raw `.bin` captures, so they can't be re-exported through the actuator path — a fresh raw capture is needed.
70	- **Corpus for Phase 2.** Many songs **at Expert** (single difficulty — see decision log), one held-out song reserved and reused across iterations so per-iteration metrics are comparable.
71	
72	- **[Deferred — not fixing now] Label↔feature pairing crosses two USB directions.** Distinct from the timestamp-burstiness issue above. The label (`PERF_REC_ACTUATOR`) is timestamped when marvin *sends* the command to fretboard; the feature (`FRETBOARD_RAW`) is timestamped when marvin *receives* the sample. The exporter forward-fills one onto the other as if they share a clock, but the two streams travel opposite directions over USB CDC with independent latency + jitter, so the reconstructed "which command was active when this ADC sample was taken" pairing has an unknown, independently-varying skew. (Overlaps the [`review.md`](review.md) "CDC + RTOS jitter in labels" risk, but is sharper: it's a *cross-stream* pairing error, not just emit-time jitter.)
73	  - **Candidate fix (deferred, pairs with the timestamp fix):** have the fretboard frame carry the **actuator bitmask it currently has applied** alongside the ADC scan (and its local sample timestamp). Then (sensor, label) is captured atomically on-device in one 240 Hz tick — no cross-stream join, zero skew. This is also the *most faithful* supervision: it's exactly the function the deployed model replaces (fretboard sees ADC → must emit the bitmask to apply now). marvin stays the teacher; we'd read its command off the wire at the point of truth instead of re-timing it on marvin. Training would then prefer fretboard-reported actuator state over `PERF_REC_ACTUATOR`.
74	  - **Cost:** fretboard wire-format growth + `FretboardRaw` schema add on marvin + a new exporter label source. See fretboard journal open-question #4. **For now we proceed with the marvin-side join** — the skew is bounded (small ms) and was present at runtime too; revisit if Phase 2 shows label noise is the accuracy ceiling (ties to [`review.md` Q4](review.md)).
75	
76	- **[CONFIRMED] Legato fret-hold was the fret-accuracy ceiling.** marvin's timing pipeline suppresses a fret release whenever a queued upcoming note needs that fret ([timing_pipeline.c:263](../../../firmware/marvin/default/src/actuator/timing_pipeline.c#L263)) — so across consecutive same-fret notes it holds the fret continuously, and in the gap the photosensor reads bright while the label stays `1` (driven by marvin's note-queue lookahead, not observable from the photo). **Proven by the `--labels=detector-fb` probe** (detector `pressed_mask` frets = clean per-note structure, no legato): on slowride-hard overfit, frets went **0.94→0.99 across the board** and the green→orange gradient flattened (loss 0.13→0.063); strum unchanged (same source). Sustains are safe under a line-263 change because a sustain holds via continuous detector `pressed` (no release edge), never reaching the suppression.
77	  - **But detector-fb is a probe, not the deployable label:** detector `pressed` (y=311) leads the photo dip by ~20 ms and releases ~220 ms *before* the strum, so a model trained on it would release the fret before strumming. Correct *structure*, wrong *timing*.
78	  - **Deployable fix (implemented 2026-06-03):** gated line-263 change in marvin's `timing_pipeline.c` — release a fret between separate notes, hold only when re-needed at/before its scheduled release (back-to-back); sustains untouched. Reflash **marvin only**, re-capture hard, export `actuator-fb` → expect ~0.99 deployable frets at correct strike-line timing. (No fretboard/wire change; `applied_mask` still == the command because there's no lazy actuator yet.)
79	
80	- **[Decided] Final actuation architecture: released commands + lazy fretboard + log the command.** For good play at higher difficulties we want (1) marvin/model to command *released-style* per-note play (clean labels — done via line-263), and (2) a fretboard **lazy actuator** that physically holds a fret across same-fret gaps (releases only on a different non-empty fret command or a no-activity timeout) so fast Expert runs don't thrash release/repress and sustains aren't dropped (a dropped sustain makes the on-screen bar disappear → corrupts the feedback loop). Because the lazy layer makes physical state ≠ command, the training label must then be the **commanded** byte: when lazy lands, add a `commanded_mask` field to the fretboard frame/record (the reserved byte absorbs it; frame 17→18 B, schema v5) and the exporter sources `actuator-fb` labels from it. **Sequencing:** line-263 now (hard mode, `applied_mask` already == command); lazy actuator + `commanded_mask` together as the Expert follow-on. Strum mechanisms (monostable + threshold + weight) already validated — onset p95 ~16.7 ms, clean uniform pulses, glitches→0; recall/precision knee to be set on the consistent line-263 dataset (bias toward recall).
81	
82	- **[Future] 3-state fret actuator (user idea).** Give each fret three states instead of two: *pressed-and-note-active*, *pressed-but-between-notes* (legato hold), and *released*. Would let the label distinguish "this fret is down because a note is here now" from "down only because it's reused soon" — directly encoding the legato hold rather than hiding it. Could be a cleaner supervision target than collapsing to a binary press. Parked until the detector-fb probe tells us whether the binary clean-structure label is enough.
83	
84	- **[Future] Dedicated fret-line (scroll-speed) sensor.** The game highway's bar/measure lines scroll past a fixed point at a frequency that *is* the scroll speed — a direct observable of the one variable (difficulty/scroll-speed) that single-row note sensors can't see. A 6th ADC channel aimed at a column where only the horizontal fret lines pass (not the colored notes) would give the model an explicit scroll-speed signal, potentially letting **one** model generalise across difficulties instead of needing per-difficulty models. Open question whether a tiny model can actually exploit it to adjust strum timing. Pairs with [`review.md` Q1/Q5](review.md) (sensor count/placement). Flag for later; v1 stays Expert-only with the existing 5 channels.
85	
86	- **Measure the photo→strum lag before fixing the window length.** With difficulty fixed, the lag is a constant we can measure (cross-correlate photo dips vs strum events in the real capture) rather than guess. Sizes the causal window precisely and turns [`review.md` Q3](review.md) from a blind sweep into a measurement + a narrow sweep around it. Lag-measurement utility is part of the Phase-2 package.
87	
88	- **[Deferred — not fixing now] Fretboard ADC samples carry no true sample timestamp.** The first real self-play capture ([`tools/marvin-perf/captures/web-20260603-104406.csv`](../../marvin-perf/captures/web-20260603-104406.csv), 251.5 s, 59 958 rows) shows the per-row `timestamp` is **bursty, not uniform 240 Hz**: ~2.9 samples cluster within <0.05 ms, then a >10 ms gap (≈12 ms burst period), with *no* rows near the expected 4.17 ms spacing. Cause: `FretboardRaw.hdr.ts_counter` is stamped at marvin's USB-CDC RX/emit time, not at the fretboard's physical sample instant; the host receives the stream in bursts and the RX task drains buffered frames back-to-back.
89	  - **Consequences:** (1) row-index windowing is mandatory (see decision log); (2) forward-filled command labels can skew by up to one burst (~12 ms / ~3 samples) near command transitions — same effect as the "CDC + RTOS jitter in labels" risk in [`review.md`](review.md); measure its magnitude in Phase 2.
90	  - **Candidate fix (deferred):** have the fretboard MCU stamp each 12-byte data frame with its own sample-time counter and carry it on the wire, so marvin records the *absolute sample-time truth* instead of RX time. That's a fretboard wire-format + firmware change (and a `FretboardRaw` schema add on marvin) — out of scope for now. **For the moment we proceed assuming regular 240 Hz intervals and window by row count.** Revisit if Phase 2 shows the label skew hurts strum-timing accuracy.

144	- First baseline (window 60, /4095 scaling) failed badly: held-out frets 80–94 %, strum recall ~30 %, timing pinned at the tolerance cap. Diagnosed as underfitting (loss monotonically falling, green crawling +4 % over 30 epochs).

A model that can't fit its own training labels is hitting **irreducible label ambiguity**, not a generalisation gap.
147	- The ~2–3-sample (8–12 ms) strum-timing floor ≈ the ~12 ms cross-stream burst interval — strongly implicating the logged label↔feature skew as the ceiling, *but* `StrumNet` is only ~590 params so **capacity is an unresolved confound.**
148	- **Decisive test result (big-model overfit, 64ch/1.3M MACs — 13× over budget, diagnostic only):** the ceiling splits in two:
149	  - **Strum *recall* is capacity-limited** — tiny model ~0.86, big model **~0.99**. Fixable with a better/bigger architecture (two-head event detector is the parameter-efficient candidate, review.md Shape D).
150	  - **Strum *timing* is data-limited** — even the 1.3M-MAC model on its own training data, with tolerance widened to 62 ms (uncensored), can't beat **p50 ~1–2 samples / p95 ~5 samples (~20 ms)**. That floor ≈ the ~12 ms cross-stream burst jitter → **confirms the label↔feature skew is the timing ceiling.** No model beats it; only the fretboard data-sync firmware fix (open-questions #3/#4) does.
151	  - **Frets** improve with capacity (yellow ~.93→~.96) but plateau short of 99% — residual is the same transition-region label skew.
152	- **Reframing the gate:** the rollout `strum p95 ≤ 20 ms` gate is almost certainly stricter than the game needs (GH/RB hit windows ≈ ±50–100 ms). 11	/* Streaming cascade is written for the fixed 3-layer, kernel-5 arch. Ring depths
12	 * below assume dilations (1, 4, 16); a different arch needs them resized. */
13	#if MODEL_N_LAYERS != 3 || MODEL_KERNEL != 5 || MODEL_N_IN != 5 || MODEL_N_OUT != 6
14	#error "model_infer_stream.c assumes 3 layers, kernel 5, 5 inputs, 6 outputs"

17	/* Streaming computes a continuous causal conv, bit-exact only with a model whose
18	 * last timestep needs no zero-padding — i.e. trained at window >= receptive field
19	 * (1 + (K-1)*(1+4+16) = 85 for this arch). Guard against deploying a shorter one. */
20	_Static_assert(MODEL_WINDOW >= 85, "streaming needs a model trained at window >= 85 (the receptive field)");

22	#define QMAX 127
23	
24	/* Each layer's ring must hold the deepest tap its consumer reads:
25	 *   q_in feeds L0 (dil 1):  (K-1)*1  = 4  -> 5
26	 *   L0   feeds L1 (dil 4):  (K-1)*4  = 16 -> 17
27	 *   L1   feeds L2 (dil 16): (K-1)*16 = 64 -> 65 */
28	#define Q_RING  5
29	#define L0_RING 17
30	#define L1_RING 65
31	
32	static const model_def_t *s_model;
33	static uint32_t s_rf;       /* receptive field; output valid once s_count >= s_rf */
34	static uint32_t s_count;    /* samples processed (for warm-up tap zeroing) */
35	
36	static int8_t s_qin[Q_RING][MODEL_N_IN];
37	static int8_t s_l0[L0_RING][MODEL_CHANNELS];
38	static int8_t s_l1[L1_RING][MODEL_CHANNELS];
39	static int s_qh, s_l0h, s_l1h;   /* index of the newest column in each ring */
40	
41	/* strum monostable (advances once per sample == 240 Hz) */
42	static uint32_t s_tick, s_hold_until, s_block_until;
43	static uint8_t  s_prev_strum;
44	
45	void model_infer_stream_set_model(const model_def_t *m)
46	{
47	    s_model = m;
48	    if (m == NULL) { return; }
49	    s_rf = 1u;
50	    for (int l = 0; l < MODEL_N_LAYERS; l++)
51	    {
52	        s_rf += (uint32_t)(MODEL_KERNEL - 1) * m->dilation[l];
53	    }
54	}

56	void model_infer_stream_init(void)
57	{
58	    s_count = 0;
59	    s_qh = s_l0h = s_l1h = 0;
60	    s_tick = 0;
61	    s_hold_until = 0;
62	    s_block_until = 0;
63	    s_prev_strum = 0;
64	    memset(s_qin, 0, sizeof(s_qin));
65	    memset(s_l0, 0, sizeof(s_l0));
66	    memset(s_l1, 0, sizeof(s_l1));

70	/* One output column (all MODEL_CHANNELS) at the newest position, reading the
71	 * previous layer's ring. Tap k reads offset (K-1-k)*dil columns back from `head`;
72	 * offsets >= s_count fall before the stream start and are zero (warm-up). Matches
73	 * the causal-left-pad convention of edge_ai.quantize.int8_sim. */
74	static void conv_col(const int8_t *w, const int32_t *b, int cin, int dil,
75	                     int32_t mult, int shift, const int8_t *ring, int ring_len,
76	                     int stride, int head, int8_t out[MODEL_CHANNELS])
77	{
78	    /* Tap ring index depends only on k (not the channels) — hoist it out of the
79	     * hot loop so the (non-power-of-two) modulo runs K times per column, not
80	     * C*Cin*K times (the M0+ has no hardware divide). -1 = before stream start. */
81	    int tap[MODEL_KERNEL];
82	    for (int k = 0; k < MODEL_KERNEL; k++)
83	    {
84	        int off = (MODEL_KERNEL - 1 - k) * dil;
85	        tap[k] = ((uint32_t)off >= s_count)
86	                     ? -1
87	                     : ((head - off) % ring_len + ring_len) % ring_len;
88	    }
89	
90	    for (int o = 0; o < MODEL_CHANNELS; o++)
91	    {
92	        int32_t acc = b[o];
93	        for (int i = 0; i < cin; i++)
94	        {
95	            const int8_t *wo = &w[(o * cin + i) * MODEL_KERNEL];
96	            for (int k = 0; k < MODEL_KERNEL; k++)
97	            {
98	                if (tap[k] < 0) { continue; }
99	                acc += (int32_t)wo[k] * (int32_t)ring[tap[k] * stride + i];
100	            }
101	        }
102	        if (acc < 0) { acc = 0; }   /* ReLU */
103	        int64_t q = ((int64_t)acc * mult + ((int64_t)1 << (shift - 1))) >> shift;
104	        if (q > QMAX) { q = QMAX; }
105	        out[o] = (int8_t)q;
106	    }
107	}
108	
109	uint8_t model_infer_stream_step(const uint16_t adc[5])
110	{
111	    const model_def_t *m = s_model;
112	    if (m == NULL) { return 0u; }
113	
114	    s_count++;
115	
116	    /* input affine -> new q_in column */
117	    s_qh = (s_qh + 1) % Q_RING;
118	    for (int c = 0; c < MODEL_N_IN; c++)
119	    {
120	        int64_t v = (int64_t)adc[c] * m->m_in[c] - m->b_in[c];
121	        int64_t q = (v + ((int64_t)1 << (m->s_in_shift - 1))) >> m->s_in_shift;
122	        if (q > QMAX) q = QMAX; else if (q < -QMAX) q = -QMAX;
123	        s_qin[s_qh][c] = (int8_t)q;
124	    }
125	
126	    /* layer 0: reads q_in ring */
127	    s_l0h = (s_l0h + 1) % L0_RING;
128	    conv_col(m->w[0], m->b[0], m->cin[0], m->dilation[0], m->req_mult[0],
129	             m->req_shift[0], &s_qin[0][0], Q_RING, MODEL_N_IN, s_qh, s_l0[s_l0h]);
130	
131	    /* layer 1: reads L0 ring */
132	    s_l1h = (s_l1h + 1) % L1_RING;
133	    conv_col(m->w[1], m->b[1], m->cin[1], m->dilation[1], m->req_mult[1],
134	             m->req_shift[1], &s_l0[0][0], L0_RING, MODEL_CHANNELS, s_l0h, s_l1[s_l1h]);
135	
136	    /* layer 2: reads L1 ring -> newest column only */
137	    int8_t l2[MODEL_CHANNELS];
138	    conv_col(m->w[2], m->b[2], m->cin[2], m->dilation[2], m->req_mult[2],
139	             m->req_shift[2], &s_l1[0][0], L1_RING, MODEL_CHANNELS, s_l1h, l2);
140	
141	    if (s_count < s_rf) { return 0u; }   /* receptive field not yet filled */
142	
143	    /* head: bit = (logit >= threshold) */
144	    uint8_t mask = 0u;
145	    int raw_strum = 0;
146	    for (int o = 0; o < MODEL_N_OUT; o++)
147	    {
148	        int32_t acc = m->head_b[o];
149	        for (int i = 0; i < MODEL_CHANNELS; i++)
150	        {
151	            acc += (int32_t)m->head_w[o * MODEL_CHANNELS + i] * (int32_t)l2[i];
152	        }
153	        int bit = (acc >= m->head_tq[o]) ? 1 : 0;
154	        if (o < 5) { if (bit) { mask |= (uint8_t)(1u << o); } }
155	        else       { raw_strum = bit; }
156	    }
157	
158	    /* strum monostable (one pulse per rising edge), advanced once per sample */
159	    int strum_out;
160	    if (m->strum_hold > 0)
161	    {
162	        uint32_t i = s_tick;
163	        if (raw_strum && !s_prev_strum && i >= s_block_until)
164	        {
165	            s_hold_until  = i + m->strum_hold;
166	            s_block_until = i + m->strum_hold + m->strum_refractory;
167	        }
168	        strum_out = (i < s_hold_until) ? 1 : 0;
169	        s_prev_strum = (uint8_t)raw_strum;
170	        s_tick++;
171	    }
172	    else
173	    {
174	        strum_out = raw_strum;
175	    }
176	    if (strum_out) { mask |= (uint8_t)(1u << 5); }
177	
178	    return mask;
179	}
180	
181	#endif /* MODEL_INFER_STREAMING */

15	 * model TRAINED AT window >= receptive field (85) — at a shorter window the
16	 * windowed model's moving zero-pad boundary would not match (see runtime.md /
17	 * edge-ai journal). Output is 0 until the receptive field has filled.
18	 *
19	 * Output bitmask matches CMD_BIT_* (bits 0..4 frets, bit 5 strum-down).

1	"""Bit-exactness gate for the STREAMING on-device inference
2	(firmware/fretboard/model_infer_stream.c).
3	
4	Streaming computes a continuous causal conv, which is bit-exact with a model
5	trained at window >= receptive field (85). So we generate a window-85 model,
6	stream the capture through model_infer_stream.c, and assert it matches the host
7	int8 reference (int8_sim at window 85) + the strum monostable, from the first
8	fully-warmed row onward.
9	
10	Needs numpy, torch, and a C compiler.

python3 - <<'PY'
# Replicate firmware s_need back-propagation (model_infer.c) to count recompute MACs.
K=5; dil=[1,4,16]; L=3
def recompute_macs(window, ch):
    need=[[0]*window for _ in range(L)]
    need[L-1][window-1]=1
    for l in range(L-1,0,-1):
        for p in range(window):
            if not need[l][p]: continue
            for j in range(K):
                pos=p-j*dil[l]
                if pos>=0: need[l-1][pos]=1
    # layer0 also defines its own needed positions already; count conv MACs
    cin=[5,ch,ch]; cout=ch
    macs=0
    for l in range(L):
        npos=sum(need[l])
        macs+=npos*cout*cin[l]*K
    macs+=ch*6  # head
    return [sum(need[l]) for l in range(L)], macs
for w in (60,85):
    for ch in (8,16):
        npos,macs=recompute_macs(w,ch)
        print(f"w={w} ch={ch}: needed_positions/layer={npos} recompute_MACs={macs}")
PY

```md
# model — StrumNet (the actual network)

What the model *is*, layer by layer, and *why* it's shaped that way. Code: [`edge_ai/model.py`](../edge_ai/model.py). For the data it consumes see [`training.md`](training.md); for the on-device int8 path see [`runtime.md`](runtime.md); for the historical decision trail (why a CNN over MPLAB ML, how the RF was sized) see the [journal](journal.md) decision log.

> **TL;DR.** A tiny causal 1D-CNN: 5 ADC channels → **3 dilated causal conv layers** `(d=1,4,16)` → a linear head on the **last timestep** → 6 sigmoids (5 frets + 1 strum). Three facts shape every choice:
> 1. It is a **predict-now** model — the head reads only the newest timestep, so the architecture is built around that timestep's **receptive field**.
> 2. The receptive field **must cover the photo→strum lag** (~48 samples / 200 ms on hard). That is why there are three dilated layers, not two: `(1,4,16)` gives **RF 85 (~354 ms)**; the old two-layer `(1,4)` was RF 21 and couldn't reach back to the cue, capping frets at ~0.86.
> 3. The model is the **timing function** marvin used to play. It learns whatever photo-dip→command delay was baked into the corpus, so it is only valid for the difficulty + timing constants it was distilled from (see [journal](journal.md) decision log).

The shipped model: `StrumNet(channels=16, kernel=5, dilations=(1,4,16))`, trained at `window=85`, int8-quantised, running standalone on the fretboard PIC32CM. The training *default* is `channels=8`; deploy passes `--channels 16` (§8).

---

## 1. Input

- **Shape:** `(batch, 5, window)` — 5 phototransistor ADC channels (G/R/Y/B/O), `window` consecutive 240 Hz samples, channels-first for `Conv1d`.
- **Normalisation:** per-channel standardise (zero-mean / unit-variance) using stats computed on the training set and saved in the checkpoint ([`data.compute_norm_stats`](../edge_ai/data.py)). **Why it's load-bearing:** the raw ADC band is narrow (idle ≈ 3900, dips ≈ 1000); naive `/4095` leaves every input clustered near 0.95 and starves gradients — the first baseline underfit until standardisation was added. At deploy this affine folds losslessly into the int8 input quantisation, so it costs nothing on device.
- **Windowing:** sliced **by row index** within a contiguous `fb_seq` run, never by the bursty `timestamp` column. Each CSV row is one true 240 Hz sample paired atomically with its label on-device; a dropped frame breaks the run so a window never stitches two non-adjacent samples (see [`data.contiguous_runs`](../edge_ai/data.py), and the [journal](journal.md) timestamp-burstiness entry).
- **At deploy:** one inference per 240 Hz tick. The window is the most recent `window` ADC samples (recompute path) or — in the streaming path — a continuous causal convolution that needs no explicit window buffer at all (§7).

## 2. Output

- **6 logits → sigmoids**, thresholded to bits: `[green, red, yellow, blue, orange, strum]`.
- **Independent per-bit** (no chord-shape coupling). Strum is the **collapsed** down|up bit; at the wire it maps to bit 5 (strum-down), bit 6 stays 0. The collapse halves the rare-class problem and reflects that alternating up/down is a human-ergonomics constraint the controller doesn't enforce ([SPEC.md §3](SPEC.md)).
- Frets thresholded at 0.5; **strum has its own threshold** (`--strum-thresh`, default 0.5) because its precision/recall curve has headroom we deliberately trade. After thresholding, the strum bit passes through the **monostable** post-processor — not part of the network, lives at deploy time (§7).

## 3. Architecture, layer by layer

\```
  5 ADC channels × W samples              input  (5, W)
  (G R Y B O), per-channel standardised
            │
            ▼
  ┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ CausalConv1d  5→C  k=5  d=1   + ReLU │  left-pad 4    → (C, W)
  └─────────────────────────────────────┘
            │
            ▼
  ┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ CausalConv1d  C→C  k=5  d=4   + ReLU │  left-pad 16   → (C, W)
  └─────────────────────────────────────┘
            │
            ▼
  ┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ CausalConv1d  C→C  k=5  d=16  + ReLU │  left-pad 64   → (C, W)
  └─────────────────────────────────────┘
            │
            ▼   last timestep only:  h[:, :, -1]          → (C,)
  ┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ Linear  C→6                          │               → 6 logits
  └─────────────────────────────────────┘
            │
            ▼   sigmoid → threshold (frets 0.5, strum tunable)
     [ G  R  Y  B  O │ strum ]
                         │
                         ▼   deploy only (not in the net): monostable one-shot
                      clean strum pulse → wire byte bit 5
\```

Parameter counts at the training default `StrumNet(channels=8, kernel=5, dilations=(1,4,16))`:

| Layer | Op | Out shape | Params |
|---|---|---|---|
| input | — | (5, W) | — |
| `CausalConv1d` 0 | Conv1d(5→8, k=5, **d=1**) + left-pad 4 | (8, W) | 5·8·5 + 8 = **208** |
| ReLU | — | (8, W) | — |
| `CausalConv1d` 1 | Conv1d(8→8, k=5, **d=4**) + left-pad 16 | (8, W) | 8·8·5 + 8 = **328** |
| ReLU | — | (8, W) | — |
| `CausalConv1d` 2 | Conv1d(8→8, k=5, **d=16**) + left-pad 64 | (8, W) | 8·8·5 + 8 = **328** |
| ReLU | — | (8, W) | — |
| take last timestep | `h[:, :, -1]` | (8,) | — |
| `head` | Linear(8→6) | (6,) | 8·6 + 6 = **54** |
| | | **total** | **918** |

The shipped 16-channel model is **3 110** params (§8). Only width changes with `--channels`; depth (3 layers) and the dilation schedule are fixed.

### Why these layers, in this order

- **1D convolution, not a dense window or an RNN.** The signal is a 5-channel time series whose informative event (a phototransistor dimming, then recovering) is *local in time but shift-equivariant* — it can occur at any offset within the window. Convolution shares weights across time, so it learns the dip→command mapping once rather than per-position; that is exactly what a dense layer over the flattened window cannot do efficiently, and it has no recurrent state to unroll on an MCU.
- **Causal padding (left-pad only).** [`CausalConv1d`](../edge_ai/model.py) left-pads by `(kernel-1)·dilation` and uses a plain `Conv1d`, so `output[t]` depends only on inputs `≤ t` — no future leakage. This is what lets us train densely on whole windows yet deploy as a streaming "predict-now" model: the training-time and deploy-time computations of `output[t]` are identical.
- **Dilation `(1, 4, 16)`, three layers.** Stacking dilated convs grows the receptive field *geometrically* for a *linear* parameter cost. Three layers at kernel 5 reach RF 85 (§4) — enough to cover the lag — for 918 params; reaching the same RF with un-dilated kernel-5 layers would need ~21 layers. The schedule `1→4→16` keeps coverage gap-free (each layer's stride is ≤ the previous layer's reach) while quadrupling reach per layer.
- **8 channels (training default).** Width sets capacity. 5→8 in layer 0 is a mild expansion; 8 is the smallest width that fit the frets well in early experiments. The strum class is sparse enough that capacity *there* is the binding constraint, which is why deploy uses 16 (§8).
- **ReLU.** Cheap, int8-friendly (a clamp at 0 in the requant), no FPU needed.
- **Linear head on the last timestep only.** The job is "what command applies *now*", so only `h[:, :, -1]` feeds the head. A temporal-pooling head would use the whole window but blur *when* an event happened — fatal for strum onset. The right way to use more of the window is to widen the RF (done), not to pool.

## 4. Receptive field — the thing the architecture is built around

Only the **last timestep** feeds the head (`h[:, :, -1]`). Its receptive field — how many of the newest input samples can influence the prediction — is:

\```
RF = 1 + Σ (kernel-1)·dilation = 1 + (5-1)·(1 + 4 + 16) = 85 samples ≈ 354 ms
\```

This single number governs the architecture, because of three consequences:

1. **The window cannot help past the RF.** Inputs older than 85 samples are convolved internally but never reach the head. This is why early `--window 96 / 128` sweeps gave nothing over `60` *when the RF was 21* — anything past the RF is discarded. The window only needs to be **≥ RF**; we train the deploy model at `window=85` (= RF) so the streaming deploy path is bit-exact (§7).

2. **The RF must cover the photo→strum lag.** The photo dip that *causes* a strum sits ~48 samples (~200 ms on hard) before the strike-line command. If the RF is shorter than that lag, the head literally cannot see the cue:

   \```
     prediction at "now" depends ONLY on the last RF samples:

       … now-48 ───────────────────────────────────── now
          │                                             │
          ▼            │<──────── RF = 85 ─────────────>│
     photo dip that    │   covers the cue ✓             │
     CAUSES this strum  └────────────────────────────────┘
     (~48 samples back, now INSIDE the receptive field)
   \```

   With the old RF-21 default the dip was *outside* the RF; the model only worked at all because slow hard-mode scrolling widened each note's occlusion enough that its tail leaked into the last 21 samples. Faster difficulties → narrower occlusion → less of it inside the RF → harder. RF 85 removes that fragility.

### Why RF 85, decided by an overfit A/B

The fret-accuracy ceiling was first diagnosed on a detector-labelled probe (labels coincident with the photo dip, so *inside* even a tiny RF — frets hit 0.99 trivially) and then predicted to bite the deployable `actuator-fb` labels (strike-line timing, ~48 samples after the dip). An overfit A/B on the line-263 `actuator-fb` data (slowride-hard, train == eval) confirmed the prediction and the fix in one shot:

| | RF 21 `(1,4)` | RF 85 `(1,4,16)` |
|---|---|---|
| frets (G/R/Y/B/O) | 0.86 / 0.84 / 0.89 / 0.91 / 0.94 | **0.97 / 0.97 / 0.98 / 0.98 / 0.99** |
| loss (plateau) | 0.309 | **0.080** |
| strum recall / precision | 0.84 / 0.53 | **0.97 / 0.82** |
| strum p95 | 20.8 ms | 16.7 ms |

RF 21 can't reach back to the cue → caps at ~0.86; RF 85 recovers to ~0.99 at ~50 k dense MACs (well under budget — §5). `(1,4,16)` is the default in [`model.py`](../edge_ai/model.py) / [`cli.py`](../edge_ai/cli.py); the dilation list is a `--dilations` flag and is stored in the checkpoint (older checkpoints fall back to `(1,4)`).

## 5. Compute cost — `count_macs` is a loose upper bound

[`count_macs`](../edge_ai/model.py) multiplies each conv's cost by the **full window** — it assumes every output position is computed, as in dense training:

| config | `count_macs` (dense, ×window) |
|---|---|
| 8 ch, window 60 | ~50 k |
| 8 ch, window 85 | ~71 k |
| 16 ch, window 85 | ~252 k |

But at deploy you only need the **last timestep**. Two on-device paths exploit that (both in firmware, both bit-exact with the host int8 sim — §7):

| path | what it computes per tick | 16 ch, window 85 |
|---|---|---|
| **recompute** ([`model_infer.c`](../../../firmware/fretboard/model_infer.c)) | only the conv positions the last timestep transitively needs (back-propagated `s_need`: 21 / 5 / 1 positions per layer) | **~16 k MACs** (~12.5 k at window 60) |
| **streaming** ([`model_infer_stream.c`](../../../firmware/fretboard/model_infer_stream.c)) | exactly **one new conv column per layer**, caching prior columns in small rings | **~3.1 k MACs** (888 at 8 ch) |

So against the ~100 k MAC/tick budget at 24 MHz, **even the 16-channel model fits comfortably**, and the streaming path clears 240 Hz with large margin. The "13× over budget" figure we once quoted was a `count_macs` artifact of the dense formula — real deploy cost is 1–2 orders of magnitude lower. We are **not** as capacity-constrained as the dense printout implies, which is what made widening to 16 channels affordable.

## 6. Training

- **Loss:** [`BCEWithLogitsLoss`](../edge_ai/train.py) with a `pos_weight` vector — 1.0 on each fret, `pos_weight` on strum (auto = inverse strum frequency, ~10–17; override with `--strum-weight`). Strum sparsity (~7–13 % on hard) otherwise collapses it to "always 0". The deploy model uses `--strum-weight 5` (below the auto value) to trim the recall bias at the source (§8).
- **Optimiser:** Adam, lr 1e-3, batch 256, 30 epochs (deploy: 50).
- **Strum label dilation** (`--strum-dilate`): optionally widen the strum positive by ±k samples in the *training* labels so a near-miss isn't fully penalised. Eval is **never** dilated.
- **Lead compensation** (`--label-lead`): shift training labels earlier by N samples to pre-empt on-device lag; eval uses the true labels. Unused in the shipped model (kept for residual-lag tuning — see [journal](journal.md) next-steps).
- **Checkpoint** stores `state_dict`, `window`, `channels`, `kernel`, `dilations`, `label_lead`, and the norm `mean`/`std` — everything needed to reconstruct the model and the input affine at eval and quantise time.

## 7. Inference & deployment (int8, on hardware)

This is **built and running standalone on the fretboard PIC32CM** (the int8 path is no longer a future "Phase 3" — it is the deployed path; see [`runtime.md`](runtime.md) and the [journal](journal.md)).

- **Quantisation — post-training, int8, essentially lossless.** [`quantize.py`](../edge_ai/quantize.py) does per-tensor symmetric int8 weights, int32 accumulators, and int64 fixed-point requant back to int8 activations (the target M0+ has no FPU, so float inference is out). Standardisation folds into an integer **input affine** `(M_in, B_in, S_in)`; output thresholding folds into an integer **compare on the head accumulator** (no on-device sigmoid: `sigmoid(x) ≥ t ⇔ x ≥ logit(t)`, so frets compare against 0 and strum against `logit(thresh)`). Measured PTQ error on slowride-hard: frets within ±0.001 of float, strum recall unchanged — so **no QAT is needed**.
- **Bit-exactness gate.** The host int8 reference (`quantize.int8_sim_*`) is asserted bit-for-bit against the actual firmware C — both the recompute path ([`tests/test_bitexact.py`](../tests/test_bitexact.py)) and the streaming path ([`tests/test_stream_bitexact.py`](../tests/test_stream_bitexact.py)), over a full capture, 0 mismatches.
- **Threshold** the 6 head accumulators (frets at 0, strum at the folded `--strum-thresh`).
- **Monostable** on the strum bit: a rising-edge-triggered one-shot (`hold` ticks high, then `refractory` ticks blocking new triggers — [`metrics.monostable`](../edge_ai/metrics.py)). It guarantees clean uniform pulses, absorbs mid-pulse glitches, and emits exactly one pulse per rising edge. A few counters; runs on the MCU. The same logic lives in both firmware paths.
- **Streaming vs recompute (why two paths).** The streaming path is bit-exact with a continuous causal conv, which only matches a model **trained at `window ≥ RF` (= 85)** — at a shorter window the moving zero-pad boundary differs. So the shipped model is trained at window 85 and deployed streaming (locks to 240 Hz, ~3 k MACs/tick). The recompute path works at any trained window but re-runs the needed positions each tick (~93 Hz at 16 ch) and is kept as the general-window fallback. Selected at build time by `MODEL_INFER_STREAMING` in [`fretboard_config.h`](../../../firmware/fretboard/fretboard_config.h).
- **Runtime weight swap.** The active model is a `model_def_t` pointer; the quantiser emits one named `model_<name>` per `--name`, several link together (shared arch dims guarded by a `_Static_assert`), and `model_infer_set_model()` swaps at runtime — the mechanism for per-difficulty models.

## 8. Capacity, limitations & open design questions

- **Deploy width = 16 channels (not the 8 ch training default).** 8 ch is capacity-limited on the sparse strum class: it overstrummed on hardware and **no threshold fixed it** — 0.85 missed real strums *and* still overstrummed, i.e. the precision/recall *curve itself* was the wall (the same signature as the early 8 ch-vs-64 ch overfit diagnostic, strum recall .86 vs .99). 16 ch lifts the whole curve (mono precision/recall .856/.969 → .942/.981) so a single threshold lands both. It's affordable because inference runs cheaply on device (§5: ~3 k MACs streaming, RAM ~4 KB of 8 KB). 32 ch would be RAM-bound, not compute-bound. The training *default* stays 8 ch; deploy passes `--channels 16`.
- **~~Receptive field too small for the lag~~ (resolved §4).** Was the headline issue; `(1,4,16)` RF-85 covers the lag (overfit frets ~0.99, held-out ≥0.96 except red). The remaining open item is generalisation polish, not the RF.
- **Red fret is the lone laggard** (held-out ~0.89 vs ≥0.96 for the others), consistent across epochs and not a corpus-coverage gap. Hypotheses (holdout variance / green-yellow neighbour confusion / `ph_red` channel quality) are listed in the [journal](journal.md) open questions; cheapest test is rotate-holdout cross-val. Carried as a known caveat — confirm it costs game score before treating it as blocking.
- **Last-timestep head** — correct for a predict-*now* model; fine as-is now the RF covers the lag. Temporal pooling would use more of the window but blur onset timing — not the right fix.
- **Per-bit independence** — chords occupy a tiny subset of 2⁶; a chord-shape head or the two-head event detector ([review.md](review.md)) is the fallback if independence caps accuracy. Not hit yet.
- **Single-difficulty validity.** The model *is* the timing function it was distilled from; mixing difficulties (or timing-constant regimes) teaches two photo→strum lags for identical inputs — ill-posed. v1 is one model per regime; multi-difficulty routes (per-difficulty models, or a scroll-speed sensor) are in [review.md](review.md) / the [journal](journal.md).
</content>
</invoke>

journal.md:49:| 2026-06-03 | **Primary path is programmatic (PyTorch), not MPLAB ML / SensiML.** MPLAB ML is demoted to an eventual *parallel demonstration* track, not the critical path. Inverts [`training.md` §5.1](training.md), which had the auto-pipeline first. | The hard part of this task is *temporal strum timing* — learning the photo-dip→strum delay over a causal window. SensiML's AutoML is feature-extraction + tree/ensemble over windowed stats: strong at "classify this window," weak at sequence/event-timing, which is exactly the part we care about (and review.md already named a causal 1D-CNN as the fallback). PyTorch gives full control over the window-length sweep (the #1 hyperparameter, [review.md Q3](review.md)), the sparse-strum class weighting, and the custom Phase-2 eval metrics (per-bit accuracy + strum-event timing distribution + visual side-by-side) the gate is judged on. Cost accepted: we own int8 quantisation + the on-device inference C in Phase 3 — tractable for a ≲1 k-MAC, 2-conv model, and the bit-exact control actually helps Phase 3's "matches host inference" gate. MPLAB ML stays valuable later as the Microchip-tooling demonstration once a known-good shape exists. |
journal.md:50:| 2026-06-03 | **v1 trains on a single difficulty — Expert.** Corpus = many songs at Expert, one held out. NOT mixed-difficulty (which reverses the old [`review.md`](review.md) "train on Easy+Med+Expert" prescription). | If the game's highway scroll speed varies with difficulty, the photo-dip→strum delay = `(pixel gap photo-row→CV-row)/scroll_speed + 220 ms` — the first term is inversely proportional to scroll speed. With 5 sensors at one row and no difficulty input, identical inputs map to different correct delays across difficulties: an ill-posed regression the model can only resolve by averaging (wrong on all). This is an *observability* gap, not a coverage gap, so more mixed data can't fix it. Single-difficulty is low-regret: if scroll speed turns out constant we lose nothing and can merge later; if it varies we've dodged the ill-posed case. Expert chosen for densest strum signal (helps the ~5.8 % rare class) and shortest delay (smallest window). Eventual structure if speed varies: one model per difficulty, difficulty selected at runtime from marvin's game-state controller. |
journal.md:99:- **`model.md` rewritten** around the design *rationale* (the user's ask: why the model is the way it is). Fixed the §3 ASCII diagram (was missing the 3rd `d=16` conv layer); added a "why these layers" subsection (1D conv vs dense/RNN, causal padding, geometric RF growth from dilation, last-timestep head); reframed §4 from the stale "RF 21 is the current default, RF 85 is a pending fix" into "RF 85 is the shipped default and here's the A/B that decided it"; updated §5 MAC table to 3 layers + both on-device paths (streaming ~3k, recompute ~16k at 16ch/w85, verified by computing `count_macs` + the firmware `s_need` cost); rewrote §7 from "Quantisation (Phase 3, not done)" to the as-built int8 path (PTQ lossless, bit-exact gate, streaming vs recompute); added `dilations`/`label_lead` to the checkpoint-contents list.
training.md:45:A training corpus is a set of marvin self-play perf-log captures **at a single difficulty** across song variety. **v1 targets `hard`** (the shipped corpus is 5 hard songs — hitme/rockroll/slowride/story/talkdirty); Expert is the eventual follow-on (see the journal — hard was picked first for slower scroll + all 5 frets). The corpus is also pinned to a single **timing regime** — `TP_STRUM_DELAY_MS=300 / TP_STRUM_PULSE_MS=40` for the current corpus — because the model *is* the photo→command timing function; mixing timing regimes is the same ill-posed averaging as mixing difficulties (see journal decision log). Each capture is exported `--labels=actuator-fb` (in-frame `applied_mask`, no cross-stream join). For deploy, all songs train with `--no-holdout`; for generalisation checks one song is held out and reused across iterations so metrics are comparable.
training.md:47:> **Why single-difficulty.** If the game highway's scroll speed varies with difficulty, the photo-dip→strum delay is `(pixel gap photo-row→CV-row)/scroll_speed + delay` — inversely dependent on scroll speed. With 5 sensors at one screen row and no difficulty input, mixing difficulties makes identical inputs map to different correct delays: an *ill-posed* regression, not merely an under-sampled one. So v1 fixes a single difficulty. If scroll speed turns out constant across difficulties, difficulties can be merged later at no cost. Eventual multi-difficulty support is one-model-per-difficulty (difficulty selected at runtime from marvin's game-state controller), or a dedicated fret-line scroll-speed sensor — see journal open questions.
runtime.md:48:Build-time `FRETBOARD_MODE` (`MODEL_DRIVEN` default, `MARVIN_DRIVEN` to restore the marvin-driven path) in [main.c](../../../firmware/fretboard/main.c). **SW0 (PB03, active-low momentary)** toggles model control at runtime; **LED0 (PB02)** lit while enabled; boots disabled (outputs released). When disabled the ISR applies mask 0 (all released) but keeps sampling, so re-enable is seamless. Eventual plan: marvin commands the difficulty/enable over serial (§ runtime weight swap).
=== Expert (non-historical) ===
rollout.md:44:Actual game scoring on a fixed song setlist (Easy + Medium + Expert), 5+ runs each: marvin-driven baseline vs. model-driven. Pass if model-driven scores within X% of baseline (X to be set by reviewer).
review.md:12:- **Multi-difficulty is ill-posed, not just out-of-distribution (resolved → single-difficulty v1).** Original guidance here was "train on Easy + Medium + Expert." That is wrong if scroll speed varies with difficulty: the photo→strum lag = `(pixel gap photo-row→CV-row)/scroll_speed + 220 ms`, so the same photo-dip pattern maps to *different* correct delays across difficulties. With 5 sensors at one row and no difficulty input, the model can't disambiguate — mixing difficulties is an ill-posed regression more data can't fix. **Resolution:** v1 trains on Expert only (see journal decision log + [training.md §4](training.md)). Per-difficulty models, or a fret-line scroll-speed sensor ([Q5](#q5-photoxistor-placement)), are the multi-difficulty routes for later.
review.md:55:- *A dedicated fret-line / scroll-speed channel* → a 6th sensor aimed at a column where only the highway's horizontal bar/measure lines pass (not the colored notes). The frequency at which lines cross it **is** the scroll speed — the exact variable single-row note sensors can't observe (see the multi-difficulty risk above). Could let one model span difficulties instead of one-per-difficulty. Open whether a tiny int8 model can actually use it to modulate strum timing. v1 stays 5-channel Expert-only; flagged for future work.
training.md:45:A training corpus is a set of marvin self-play perf-log captures **at a single difficulty** across song variety. **v1 targets `hard`** (the shipped corpus is 5 hard songs — hitme/rockroll/slowride/story/talkdirty); Expert is the eventual follow-on (see the journal — hard was picked first for slower scroll + all 5 frets). Each capture is exported `--labels=actuator-fb` (in-frame `applied_mask`, no cross-stream join).
